summary: Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Paris, the Royal Conservatory of Brussels, and under Sylvain Lévi, Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

An Indologist and archaeologist, Alexandra van der Geer studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar. She held posts at Leiden University, the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, and IIAS.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as a professor of rhetorics at the Lycée Charlemagne (~1826–1835), an inspector for the Académie de Paris (1835–1854), and a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1835–1854).

Alexey Belyakov is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed postgraduate study at Amur State University. His career includes posts at the Center for the Preservation of Historical and Cultural Heritage of the Amur Region, Amur State University, Heihe University, and Changchun University.
Alexis Cordier was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He pursued medical studies at the École de santé navale and the University of Bordeaux from approximately 1890 to 1894.

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He spent his career at the University of Oxford as Lecturer in Sanskrit (~1977–1992) and Professor (~1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner. He spent his career at George Washington University as assistant, associate, and Columbian Professor (1968–1981).
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alf Torp was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Oslo and the University of Leipzig under Sophus Bugge, Ernst Windisch, and Georg Curtius. He served as Professor eo. for Sanskrit and Comparative Linguistics at Oslo (1894–1914).

Alfons Fürst is a scholar of religious studies and archaeology who studied at the universities of Regensburg and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He served as a professor at the University of Münster from 2000, later serving as dean (2008–2010).

Alfons Hilka was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Breslau, Berlin, and Poitiers under Adolf Tobler, Carl Appel, and Alfred Hillebrandt. He held posts at Breslau, Bonn, and Greifswald before becoming professor at Göttingen in 1921.

Alfons Klaus Weidert was a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (~1968–1971). He later held a research position with the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (~1980–1984) and served as a Privatdozent at Kiel University (1982).

Alfons Nehring was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Otto Schrader. He taught at Breslau, Würzburg, Marquette, and Fordham, ultimately serving as ordinary professor of Indogermanistik at the University of Würzburg (1952–1958).

Alfons Väth worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught English and Indian history at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (~1912–1925), which he founded in 1913, and served as editor of Die Katholischen Missionen from 1918 to 1925.

Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied in Rome and Paris under Carlo Formichi, Giuseppe Tucci, Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou. She became docent (1949) and Professor of Sanskrit (1951) at Sapienza University of Rome.

Alfred Bloch was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Basel. He spent his career at Basel, becoming a Privatdozent in 1942 and serving as Lehrbeauftragter für Indogermanistik and Lecturer of Hebrew from 1949 to 1982.

Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who studied at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He taught religion at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), served at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and was Dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).
Alfred Chilton Pearson was a linguist who studied under John Peile at Christ's College, Cambridge, beginning in 1879, after earlier studies at Highgate School and King's College School.
Alfred Collins is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Sri Padmanabha Menon. He held an attested post at the Pacifica Graduate Institute in 2019.

Alfred Cooper Woolner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell at Trinity College, Oxford. In 1903, he became Principal of Oriental College and Dean of University Instruction at the University of the Punjab, serving until 1936.
